messages:
ash: Heads-up — CI perf job `quant-int8-load` (post-merge abc1234) shows a consistent ~+18-22% p50 latency regression compared to baseline. Repro steps in the job link below.

perf-bot: perf/regression-checker found delta +19% p50, job: https://ci.redwood/int8/3141592653 — logs attached. :warning:

jordan: Ack. Is this only on the int8 profile? Any FP8 or int4 baselines affected?

sara: I scanned the job matrix quickly: only int8-optimized kernels show the regression. FP8 job green. int4 noisy but within noise.

oliver: Quick profiling (local) shows a new hotspot in dequant path after the abc1234 merge. Stack sample:

```
# flame snippet (top 3)
- dequant_copy_loop + 42%\n- kv_cache_touch + 18%\n- kernel_selector_dispatch + 15%\n```

ash: That matches the CI trace. The merge touched kernel selector heuristics and added a new fallback path for uncommon alignments. Maybe the fallback runs dequant in a slower path.

jordan: Reproduced locally with stress harness:
```
./scripts/stress_infer --model gordong-7b-int8 --seq 1024 --concurrency 8 --profile
```
Baseline (pre-abc1234): p50 42ms
Post-merge: p50 51ms (+21%).

sara: Can you dump the allocator and heap-walk counts? I suspect extra copy path allocs.

oliver: Dumped counts:
```
alloc_moves: 124k -> 318k
memcpy_dequant_calls: 0.9M -> 1.7M
kv_touch_missed: 12% -> 13.5%
```
So dequant calls doubled.

ash: Interesting — kernel_selector now prefers the 'packed-dequant' kernel only when alignment==0; otherwise it does scalar-dequant which does byte-by-byte copy. abc1234 added the alignment check but our quant packer sometimes produces misaligned buffers based on batch padding.

jordan: Proposal: tighten kernel selector to accept small misalignments (<=16) and route to packed-dequant, or prepare an aligned staging buffer in the packer for the hot path. Which is lower risk?

sara: Aligned staging buffer is simple but adds one copy for aligned case too unless we make it conditional. The selector patch is smaller but touches dispatch logic, risk for other models.

ash: Can we bisect to the exact commit in the merge that introduced the alignment guard? I started a git bisect: range def: abc1200..abc1300.

jordan: I ran git bisect locally — culprit is abc1234 (the merge commit) -> diff: `kernel_selector: prefer safe scalar for odd alignments` (lines removed/added). Attached patch idea to relax to <=16.

oliver: I instrumented a quick patch in runtime that treats misalign<=16 as aligned and reran stress harness: p50 back to 43ms. No correctness failures in small sample.

ci-bot: Rerun requested: `quant-int8-load` with quick patch branch `fix/int8-align-tolerance` queued.

perf-bot: Quick smoke results: p50 delta now +2% on one run (within noise). Need full CI to be sure.

ash: Next steps: 1) open a small PR with the selector tolerance + unit test for alignment cases, 2) run full perf matrix, 3) if green, backport to canary. Who wants the PR?

jordan: I'll put up the PR and include the microbench. Will add a guard to avoid extra copies and add a test that packs with batch paddings that used to misalign.

sara: Also add a telemetry gauge for memcpy_dequant_calls so we can catch similar regressions in future.

oliver: FYI, we should also add a perf regression alert on allocation moves for dequant path. That was the fastest signal here.

ash: Great. Thanks all — please reference this thread in the PR and ping #eng-runtime when CI is ready. :thumbsup:
